short_name: SEC Cybersecurity Disclosure - Reg S-K Item 106
summary: Annual 10-K disclosure of cyber risk management processes, strategy, material effects, board oversight and management's role and expertise.
applies_to: SEC registrants filing Forms 10-K (foreign private issuers have parallel 20-F requirements).
size_thresholds: Applies regardless of size. Smaller reporting companies got a later compliance date for the Form 8-K item only.

summary: Disclose a material cybersecurity incident within four business days after determining it is material (delay of up to 30 days, extendable, only if the U.S. Attorney General determines disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety).
size_thresholds: Smaller reporting companies received an additional 270 days to comply after the rule became effective.

short_name: SOX Section 404 - Management assessment of internal controls
summary: Annual internal control report on ICFR. IT general controls (access, change management, operations) are in scope for auditors.
applies_to: SEC issuers filing annual reports under Exchange Act 13(a) or 15(d).
size_thresholds: Section 404(b) auditor attestation does not apply to issuers that are neither large accelerated nor accelerated filers (15 U.S.C. 7262(c)).

summary: Notify the Federal Reserve of a 'notification incident' no later than 36 hours after determining it occurred.
applies_to: U.S. bank holding companies, savings and loan holding companies, state member banks, and U.S. operations of FBOs.

short_name: Interagency Guidelines Establishing Information Security Standards
summary: Board-approved information security program for customer information (GLBA 501(b)): risk assessment, oversight of service providers, response programs.
applies_to: Customer information of bank holding companies and their nonbank subsidiaries/affiliates under Federal Reserve supervision (excluding brokers, dealers, insurers, investment companies and advisers).

summary: Plan-level privacy/security duties; the plan sponsor must firewall PHI from employment decisions.
applies_to: Holding companies that sponsor self-insured group health plans. The plan is a covered entity and the sponsor's access is limited by 164.504(f).
size_thresholds: A plan with fewer than 50 participants that is administered by the employer itself is excluded from 'group health plan' (45 CFR 160.103).
status: In force. The eCFR still shows the 2024 reproductive health care amendments (164.502(a)(5)(iii)); a federal court reportedly vacated them in June 2025. That status is not confirmed from a .gov source here.

summary: Would require covered entities to report covered cyber incidents to CISA within 72 hours and ransom payments within 24 hours (proposed 226.5).
applies_to: Holding companies whose subsidiaries meet a sector criterion, e.g., proposed 226.2(b)(7) covers all U.S. bank holding companies and S&L holding companies regulated by the Federal Reserve.
size_thresholds: Size-based prong: exceeds the SBA size standard for its NAICS code.
status: PROPOSED ONLY. NPRM 89 FR 23644 (Apr 4, 2024). CISA held town halls (Feb 13 and May 26, 2026 notices) to refine scope. Fall 2025 Unified Agenda targeted a final rule for 09/2026. As of 2026-09-25 no final rule is in the Federal Register; CISA says it 'continues to work on the final rule.' Reporting is not yet mandatory.
